import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.11

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Is it true that every finitely presented group contains either a free subsemigroup on two
generators or a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?

A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many generators
and finitely many defining relators. Two elements $a, b$ of a group generate a free subsemigroup
on two generators if distinct nonempty positive words in $a$ and $b$ always represent distinct
group elements, i.e. the canonical semigroup homomorphism from the free semigroup of rank $2$ is
injective. The "or" is inclusive.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.11»

/-- A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite
set of generators `α` and a finite set of relators `rels : Set (FreeGroup α)`. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type) (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)),
    Finite α ∧ rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- Two elements $a, b$ of a group $G$ generate a free subsemigroup on two generators if the
semigroup homomorphism from the free semigroup on two generators sending the generators to
$a$ and $b$ is injective, i.e. $a$ and $b$ satisfy no nontrivial positive-word relation. -/
def IsFreeSubsemigroupPair {G : Type*} [Group G] (a b : G) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (FreeSemigroup.lift ![a, b])

/-- A group given by a finite presentation is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {α : Type} [Finite α] {rels : Set (FreeGroup α)}
    (h : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨α, rels, inferInstance, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- No two elements of a commutative group generate a free subsemigroup on two generators. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem not_isFreeSubsemigroupPair_of_commGroup {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] (a b : G) :
    ¬ IsFreeSubsemigroupPair a b := by
  intro h
  have := @h (.of 0 * .of 1) (.of 1 * .of 0) (by simp [mul_comm])
  simp [FreeSemigroup.ext_iff] at this

/--
Is it true that every finitely presented group contains either a free subsemigroup on two
generators or a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?

Here `Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G` means that `G` has a nilpotent subgroup of finite index.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.11» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G →
      (∃ a b : G, IsFreeSubsemigroupPair a b) ∨ Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.11»

modeling_decisions: Groups are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the Kourovka file idiom (1_40, 19_25); this loses nothing since finitely presented groups are countable and the definition of `IsFinitelyPresented` works for any universe.

`IsFinitelyPresented G` is `∃ (α : Type) (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)), Finite α ∧ rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)`, i.e. isomorphic to a group with finitely many generators and finitely many relators (α may be empty, giving the trivial group, which is harmless).

'Free subsemigroup on two generators' is read literally as a free *semigroup* (not monoid) of rank 2: `Function.Injective (FreeSemigroup.lift ![a, b])`, i.e. distinct nonempty positive words in a, b give distinct elements. This forces a ≠ b and is equivalent to the free-monoid version (a nonempty word equal to 1 would give w*a = a, contradicting injectivity).

'Nilpotent subgroup of finite index' uses Mathlib's `Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G`, definitionally `∃ N : Subgroup G, Group.IsNilpotent N ∧ N.FiniteIndex`, exactly the form requested by the decomposition table.
The disjunction is the inclusive `∨`, as the table specifies.
Two `@[category API]` tests are included: `PresentedGroup rels` with finite data is finitely presented, and no pair in a commutative group is a free subsemigroup pair.

/-!

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Is it true that every finitely presented group contains either a free
subsemigroup on two generators or a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?

A group is finitely presented if it has a presentation with finitely many
generators and finitely many relators. A group contains a free subsemigroup
on two generators if it has elements $a, b$ such that distinct non-empty
positive words in $a, b$ give distinct elements of the group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.11»

/-- A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a presented group
$\langle \alpha \mid R \rangle$ with a finite set of generators $\alpha$ and a
finite set of relators $R$. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type) (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)),
    Finite α ∧ rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- A group $G$ contains a free subsemigroup on two generators if there are
$a, b \in G$ such that the semigroup homomorphism from the free semigroup on
two generators sending the generators to $a$ and $b$ is injective, that is,
$a$ and $b$ satisfy no non-trivial relation between positive words. -/
def ContainsFreeSubsemigroupOnTwoGenerators (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : G, Function.Injective (FreeSemigroup.lift ![a, b])

/-- A presented group with finitely many generators and relators is finitely
presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {α : Type} [Finite α]
    {rels : Set (FreeGroup α)} (h : rels.Finite) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨α, rels, inferInstance, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- A commutative group contains no free subsemigroup on two generators. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem not_containsFreeSubsemigroupOnTwoGenerators_of_isMulCommutative
    (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsMulCommutative G] :
    ¬ ContainsFreeSubsemigroupOnTwoGenerators G := by
  rintro ⟨a, b, h⟩
  have := @h (FreeSemigroup.of 0 * FreeSemigroup.of 1) (FreeSemigroup.of 1 * FreeSemigroup.of 0)
    (by simp [mul_comm])
  simp [FreeSemigroup.of] at this

/--
Is it true that every finitely presented group contains either a free
subsemigroup on two generators or a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?

Here "or" is inclusive, and a free subsemigroup on two generators means a
subsemigroup freely generated by two elements $a, b$, i.e. distinct non-empty
positive words in $a, b$ represent distinct elements of $G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.11» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G →
      ContainsFreeSubsemigroupOnTwoGenerators G ∨
        ∃ H : Subgroup G, H.FiniteIndex ∧ Group.IsNilpotent H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.11»

/-!
# Conjecture 10.11

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Is it true that every finitely presented group contains either a free
subsemigroup on two generators or a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.11»

/--
A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle \alpha \mid R \rangle$ given by a finite set $\alpha$ of generators and a
finite set $R$ of relators, i.e. to `PresentedGroup rels` for some finite type `α`
and some finite set `rels : Set (FreeGroup α)`.
-/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type) (_ : Finite α) (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/--
A group given by a finite presentation is finitely presented.
-/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {α : Type} [Finite α] {rels : Set (FreeGroup α)}
    (hrels : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨α, ‹_›, rels, hrels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/--
A finitely presented group is finitely generated.
-/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨α, _, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : Group.FG (FreeGroup α) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of α, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.symm.toMonoidHom.comp (PresentedGroup.mk rels))
    (e.symm.surjective.comp (PresentedGroup.mk_surjective rels))

/--
Is it true that every finitely presented group contains either a free subsemigroup on
two generators or a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?

Here "$G$ contains a free subsemigroup on two generators" means that there are
$a, b \in G$ such that the semigroup homomorphism from the free semigroup on two
generators to $G$ sending the generators to $a$ and $b$ is injective, i.e. distinct
nonempty positive words in $a$ and $b$ represent distinct elements of $G$. The "or" is
inclusive.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.11» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G →
      (∃ a b : G, Function.Injective (FreeSemigroup.lift ![a, b])) ∨
      (∃ H : Subgroup G, H.FiniteIndex ∧ Group.IsNilpotent H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.11»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot table matches the statement, and the formalization follows its notes (finite generators and finitely many relators via `PresentedGroup`, inclusive or, genuinely free semigroup of rank 2 via injectivity of the canonical map from the free semigroup on two generators).
modeling_decisions: Finitely presented is modeled up to isomorphism: `Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)` with `α : Type`, `Finite α`, `rels.Finite`. This is the standard meaning (having *some* finite presentation) and is independent of the chosen generating set.

'Contains a free subsemigroup on two generators' is rendered as `∃ a b : G, Function.Injective (FreeSemigroup.lift ![a, b])`, injectivity of the semigroup hom `FreeSemigroup (Fin 2) →ₙ* G`. This is equivalent to G having a subsemigroup isomorphic to the free semigroup of rank 2 (image of the injective hom / images of the two generators of such a subsemigroup). I verified in scratch tests that `a = b`, commutativity of G, and a sample positive-word relation `a*b = b*a*a` each refute this condition. `FreeSemigroup` (nonempty words) rather than `FreeMonoid` was used to match 'subsemigroup'; in a group the two readings are equivalent anyway (a positive word equal to 1 would give w*a = a).

The disjunction is inclusive `∨`, as the notebook's 'either ... or' is standardly read in this dichotomy (e.g. ℤ² × F₂-type examples make exclusivity false anyway).
Quantification over `G : Type` (universe 0) follows the idiom of the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 20_76).

The bespoke definition and its two API lemmas are kept in the problem file (as instructed to write only to candidate.lean); a reviewer may prefer moving `IsFinitelyPresented` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as a reusable definition.
